messages.text:
I found the reference binary path and confirmed the existing `compile.sh` is only a placeholder that checks for `executable`.

To match the evaluator, the implementation needs a Python `executable` at root plus a Windows-safe `compile.sh` that does not leave a higher-priority broken wrapper.

commands.commandLine: $ref=(Get-Content .\REFERENCE_BINARY.txt -TotalCount 1); $cases=@('-c "1 + 2"','-c "[1 2 3] | math sum"','-c "[[name,age]; [bob, 3], [ann, 4]] | to json --raw"','-c "\"abc\" | str upcase"','-c "\"a,b`n1,2\" | from csv | to json --raw"','-c "{a: 1, b: [2 3]} | to json --raw"','--version'); foreach($c in $cases){ Write-Host "CASE $c"; $p=Start-Process -FilePath $ref -ArgumentList $c -NoNewWindow -Wait -PassThru -RedirectStandardOutput .tura_out.txt -RedirectStandardError .tura_err.txt; Write-Host "STATUS $($p.ExitCode)"; Write-Host "OUT<<<"; Get-Content .tura_out.txt -Raw; Write-Host ">>>ERR<<<"; Get-Content .tura_err.txt -Raw; Write-Host ">>>" }
